name: Better Food
who: Independent organic grocer with four Bristol shops, each paired with its own cafe.
why: A fixture of Bristol's ethical-food scene since the early 2000s, known for the shop-plus-cafe format at every branch.
takeaway: Go for the shop-plus-cafe format at every branch — a fixture of Bristol's ethical-food scene since the early 2000s.

name: Wild Oats
who: Long-running independent wholefoods shop in Bristol, trading since the 1970s-80s wholefood movement.
why: One of the older independent health-food shops still trading in a city famous for them.
takeaway: Go for one of the oldest independent wholefood shops still trading in a city famous for them.

name: Ruohonjuuri
who: Finland's leading health-food chain, trading since 1982, selling natural foods, supplements and organic cosmetics.
why: Set the template for health-food retail in Finland and still runs the country's widest store network in the category.
takeaway: Go for Finland's widest health-food network — natural foods, supplements and organic cosmetics under one template.

name: La Louve
who: Member-run food cooperative in the Park Slope Food Coop mold, open since 2016; members work shifts in exchange for low prices.
why: France's best-known food co-op, widely written up abroad as a working alternative to conventional grocery retail.
takeaway: France's best-known food co-op — go to see the Park-Slope-style work-a-shift-for-lower-prices model in action.

name: BEES coop
who: Member-owned cooperative supermarket in Brussels, open since 2015, run on volunteer member shifts.
why: Belgium's flagship food co-op and a reference point for the member-run grocery model in continental Europe.
takeaway: Belgium's flagship food co-op — go to see the volunteer-shift model that defines member-run grocery in Europe.

name: SuperBioMarkt
who: Regional organic supermarket chain headquartered in Munster, selling groceries, produce and household goods.
why: One of the established organic-supermarket names in western Germany, running for decades under one brand.
takeaway: Go for an established western-German organic-supermarket name that's run under one brand for decades.

name: Country Life
who: Health-food store, bakery and vegetarian restaurant chain that says it was there when organic food first reached the Czech market; six shops plus restaurants and a cafe in and around Prague.
why: A pioneer of the Czech organic-food movement, still operating its original Old Town shop and restaurant today.
takeaway: Go for the original Old Town shop and restaurant that pioneered organic food reaching the Czech market.

name: iCOOP Natural Dream
who: Retail arm of iCOOP, South Korea's largest consumer cooperative federation, selling organic and natural foods to its member base.
why: Anchors one of Asia's biggest working consumer co-op networks, with a store finder pointing to dozens of member locations.
takeaway: Go to see the retail face of one of Asia's biggest working consumer co-op networks.

name: Leezen
who: Taiwanese organic and sustainable-goods retail chain (Chinese: Li Ren) run as a social enterprise, with stores island-wide.
why: One of Taiwan's most recognized organic grocery names, built explicitly around ethical sourcing rather than just product range.
takeaway: Go for ethical sourcing built into the business model, not just the product range, at Taiwan's known organic chain.

name: Bin Inn
who: New Zealand bulk wholefoods chain with stores nationwide, trading over 35 years, built around fill-your-own-container bulk bins.
why: Pioneered the bulk-bin, low-packaging shopping format in New Zealand well before it became a trend elsewhere.
takeaway: Go for fill-your-own-container bulk bins — New Zealand's low-packaging pioneer, decades before it became a trend.

name: Piko Wholefoods
who: Member-owned wholefoods cooperative store trading in Christchurch since the mid-1970s.
why: One of the longest-running food co-ops in New Zealand, still run on member ownership.
takeaway: Go for one of New Zealand's longest-running food co-ops, still run entirely on member ownership.

name: Paddock To Pantry
who: Family-run New Zealand grocer (formerly trading as Huckleberry) with two physical shops plus nationwide delivery.
why: A boutique NZ-owned grocer that rebranded but kept its curated, farm-forward wholefoods focus.
takeaway: Go for a curated, farm-forward wholefoods focus that survived this boutique grocer's rebrand from Huckleberry.

name: Healthy Options
who: Long-running Philippine health-food and supplement retail chain with mall-based stores nationwide.
why: The best-known name in Philippine health-food retail, built over decades of mall presence.
takeaway: Go for the best-known name in Philippine health-food retail, built on decades of mall presence.

name: ThreeSixty
who: Upscale organic supermarket chain in Hong Kong with several stores carrying imported organic and specialty goods.
why: The reference organic supermarket for Hong Kong's health-conscious and expat shoppers.
takeaway: Go for the imported organic and specialty goods that make this Hong Kong's reference health-food supermarket.

name: Angelic Organic Grocer
who: Melbourne health-food grocer and juice bar combining a wholefoods shop with a smoothie/juice counter.
why: A go-to stop for Melbourne's fitness and wellness crowd, more destination than plain grocery run.
takeaway: Go for the smoothie counter that makes this more destination than plain grocery run for Melbourne's fitness crowd.

name: Fresh Earth Store
who: Independent organic grocer and cafe in Johannesburg's Rosebank/Craighall area, running for over a decade.
why: One of Johannesburg's established organic-food destinations, combining a grocery with a sit-down cafe.
takeaway: Go for the sit-down cafe attached to one of Johannesburg's established organic-grocery destinations.
